summary: This file is a unittest suite for the robot pet family: it checks that a RobotPet clamps its battery into the 0-100 range, and that each subclass (RobotCat, RobotBird, RobotDog) has its own show_talent message while still inheriting charge from the parent class.

lines.code: from pet_talents import RobotPet, RobotCat, RobotBird, RobotDog
lines.text: The classes under test live in a separate module named pet_talents.py, so the test file imports them; keeping tests apart from the code they exercise is the normal layout.
Each group of related tests gets its own TestCase subclass, which is how unittest discovers and organises tests.
The ellipsis stands for the earlier RobotPet tests from the previous section, which are not reprinted here; replace it with those test methods when you type the file out.
Test names start with test_ so unittest picks them up automatically, and the rest of the name says exactly which rule is being checked.
Passing a negative battery deliberately probes the boundary of the allowed range rather than an ordinary value.
The constructor is expected to raise any value below zero up to zero instead of storing the bad number.
The other end of the clamp: anything over 100 must be capped at a full battery.
setUp runs before every test method in the class, giving each test a fresh object so one test cannot leave state behind that affects another.
Storing the pet on self makes it available to every test method in this class.
assertIn checks that the returned text mentions the pet's name, without pinning the test to the exact wording of the whole sentence.
This guards against a method that prints instead of returning, or that returns None by accident.
The point of overriding show_talent is that the cat says something cat-specific, so the test fails if the subclass falls back to the parent's generic message.
Setting the battery directly puts the object into a known starting state for the charge calculation.
charge is defined on RobotPet, so this checks that the subclass really inherits the parent's behaviour.
Fifty plus twenty stays under the cap, so the expected result is a plain addition.
This guard means the tests run when the file is executed directly, but not when it is imported by something else.
unittest.main finds every TestCase in the file, runs all their test methods, and prints a summary of passes and failures.
